newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL SHRS SEEN UP A TAD IN WEAK, VOLATILE TRADE.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL SHRS SEEN UP A TAD IN WEAK, VOLATILE TRADE.

text.p: Brazil stocks may open up after Friday's drop but trade is expected to be weak and volatile ahead of futures and options expiries while prices take their cue from Wall Street due to a lack of local news, they said.
"If New York doesn't do poorly, we should have a pretty good day," said John Carioba of local Indusval brokerage.
The Sao Paulo bolsa's Bovespa index of 47 most-traded shares ended off 1.57 percent Friday at 12,128 points in thin trade of 547.4 million reais ($506.8 million).
Brokers said prices may edge higher at the open in a technical reaction to Friday's declines.
But trade is likely to remain sluggish as many foreign investors avoid the rising volatility ahead of Wednesday's futures expiry and options settlements on August 18, they said.
Moreover, a lack of local news means stocks will be hostage to overseas stock movements. "Eyes will be on markets abroad," said a dealer at local Fonte brokerage.
Dealers said they were concerned about Friday's thin trade and by low volumes expected this week, especially the lack of liquidity in second-tier stocks.
"It means that we are still too concentrated in one stock and maybe it's worse now than before," a local broker said, referring to benchmark Telebras .

Telebras shares and options regularly account for 60 to 65 percent of total bolsa turnover. But that percentage may have been even higher in recent sessions, possibly due to the approach of futures and options expirations, traders said.
